answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a staked trust graph. Each agent locks a bond in a public registry to mint a single voting vertex, and that bond is slashed if the vertex is ever proven a duplicate. Endorsements begin in a small lagoon of verified agents; every new identity must be vouched for by one already staked, so trust climbs a narrow ledge instead of spreading for free. An attacker who wants k fake voices must lock k separate bonds and recruit k genuine endorsers, so the cost grows linearly with the size of the attack, and any caught duplicate burns the whole stake.
